source_text:
Ἄκουσον τοῦ
Ἰωάννου λέγοντος· Τεκνία, ἐσχάτη ὥρα ἐστίν. Ὁρᾷς ὅτι τῇ ἑνδεκάτῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ τοῦ
ἀμπελῶνος δεσπότης, εὑρὼν ἀργοὺς ἐμισθώσατο. Τίνες οὗτοι οἱ ἀργοί; Ἡμεῖς οἱ ἀπὸ
τῶν ἐθνῶν· ἀργοὶ γὰρ ἦμεν ἀπὸ θεογνωσίας, ἀργοὶ ἀπὸ ἔργων ἀγαθῶν. Καὶ λέγει
αὐτοῖς· Τί ἑστήκατε ὧδε ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀργοί· Ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν ἀπ' ἀρχῆς
κτίσεως κόσμου, ἕως τῆς ἐπιδημίας αὐτοῦ χρόνον ἐσήμανεν· ἕως γὰρ τότε ἀργὰ ἦν
τὰ ἔθνη, Θεὸν μὴ εἰδότα· Οὐδεὶς γὰρ, φασὶν, ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο. Εὐγνώμονα τὰ ἔθνη·
τῷ γὰρ οὐδεὶς αὐτὰ ἐμισθώσατο, οὐ νόμοι, οὐ προφῆται· τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐκεῖνοι
ἀπεστάλησαν, οὐ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν· διὸ καλῶς λέγουσιν, ὅτι Οὐδεὶς ἡμᾶς ἐμισθώσατο.
Ἀλλὰ ἀγαθὸς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης, Ὑπάγετε γὰρ καὶ ὑμεῖς, φησὶν, ἐργάσασθαι ἐν τῷ
ἀμπελῶνι, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν ᾗ δίκαιον, δώσω ὑμῖν.
thought_title: The idle Gentiles hired at the eleventh hour
orientation: Cyril is explaining the eleventh-hour hiring in the parable, identifying the idle laborers as the Gentiles and quoting John and the landowner's words.
pass_a_gloss: Hear John saying: Little children, it is the last hour. You see that at the eleventh hour the master of the vineyard went out, found idle people, and hired them. Who are these idle people? We who are from the Gentiles; for we were idle from knowledge of God, idle from good works. And he says to them: Why do you stand here idle the whole day? The whole day he indicated the time from the beginning of the creation of the world until his coming; for until then the Gentiles were idle, not knowing God. For no one, they say, hired us. The Gentiles are reasonable; for by the fact that no one hired them, no laws, no prophets; to Israel those were sent, not to the Gentiles; therefore they say well that No one hired us. But the landowner is good, for Go, you also, he says, to work in the vineyard, and whatever is right, I will give you.

choices.why: The brief's cast lists δεσπότης Θεός for God; here δεσπότης alone refers to the vineyard's master, and 'master' keeps the authority sense without the banned 'householder'.
The glossary mandates 'idle' for ἀργοί, representing the Gentiles before Christ.
The glossary mandates 'coming' for ἐπιδημία, referring to Christ's incarnation.
The glossary mandates 'landowner' for οἰκοδεσπότης, representing God as lord of the world.
The glossary mandates 'Gentiles' for ἔθνη, as distinct from Israel.

pass_b_english: Listen to John when he says, “Little children, it is the last hour” (1 John 2:18). You see that when the master of the vineyard went out at the eleventh hour, he found idle people and hired them. Who are these idle people? We are—we who come from the Gentiles. For we were idle from the knowledge of God, idle from good works. And he says to them, “Why have you been standing here idle all day?” “All day” signified the whole span of time from the beginning of the creation of the world until his coming. For until then the Gentiles were idle, not knowing God. “No one,” they say, “has hired us.” The Gentiles are reasonable in saying this, for no one had hired them—no laws, no prophets. Those were sent to Israel, not to the Gentiles. That is why they rightly say, “No one has hired us.” But the landowner is good, for he says, “You also go and work in the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.”

last_rejected.quote: The Gentiles are reasonable in saying this
last_rejected.why: English hides that Cyril addresses the Gentiles directly, not about them.
last_rejected.fix: You Gentiles are reasonable in saying this
last_rejected.ruling: Εὐγνώμονα τὰ ἔθνη is nominative plural; 'The Gentiles are reasonable' correctly renders it, not direct address.

last_rejected.why: Greek has singular 'law' (νόμοι is likely error for νόμος), not plural 'laws'.
last_rejected.ruling: Source text reads οὐ νόμοι (plural); translator correctly renders given text. Emending source is not a translation error.
